title: I used GPT-6.1 Sol to build Goods Sort: PACKING PUZZLE — a sorting game you can play right here on Reddit
author: Reasonable_Damage_18
selftext:
Hi r/aigamedev! I’m the developer of Goods Sort: PACKING PUZZLE, a goods-sorting puzzle you can play directly on Reddit.

I used GPT-6.1 Sol as my AI development tool to help build and refine the game. I guided the design and worked through the implementation in small iterations, checking how changes felt in the running game. My biggest takeaway was to treat each AI-assisted change as a starting point: try it in the actual game, see what works, then refine it.

I’ve attached a short gameplay video. If you’d like to try the game, it’s here:

[https://www.reddit.com/r/goods\_sort\_packing/comments/1xdvulz/goods\_sortpacking\_puzzle/](https://www.reddit.com/r/goods_sort_packing/comments/1xdvulz/goods_sortpacking_puzzle/)

For other developers using coding models: after an AI-assisted change, what do you check first in the running game—core mechanics, input behavior, or visual feedback?
